draft.title: Land degradation
card: Land degradation is when land becomes less able to grow crops or feed livestock. It lowers how much food a farm can produce.
Soil erosion
wind or water carries away the topsoil, the fertile top layer where plants grow best.
Salinity
salt builds up in the soil or water and harms plants. Rising groundwater can bring salt to the surface.
Desertification
dry land turns into desert-like land that can no longer support much plant growth.
draft.remember: Degraded land grows less food, and farming practices are often a cause.

a.q: Which of these is an example of land degradation?
opts: Salt building up in a wheat paddock so crops grow poorly
Farmers adding more crop varieties to a healthy paddock
A paddock being left with grass cover through a dry season
Rain soaking into soil that is covered by plants
a.why: Salt building up in the soil harms plants, so the paddock can grow less food. That is salinity, a form of land degradation. Adding crop varieties does not damage the land's ability to grow food.
a.clue: Which one leaves the land able to grow less?

b.q: Too many sheep graze a paddock in Western Australia for years. Plants are eaten down and the bare topsoil blows away in strong winds. What is the best description of this?
opts: Overgrazing leading to soil erosion
Poor irrigation leading to salinity
Clearing leading to desertification only
Salinity leading to overgrazing
b.why: Too many sheep removed the plant cover, which is overgrazing, and wind then carried off the topsoil, which is soil erosion. Salinity is about salt in the soil, and nothing in the case mentions salt or irrigation.
b.clue: Name the cause first, then what happened to the topsoil.

proposal.title: Land degradation
card: Land degradation is damage that leaves land less able to grow crops or feed livestock. It is often caused by clearing (removing native plants), overgrazing (too many animals) and poor irrigation.
Soil erosion
wind or water carries away the topsoil, the fertile top layer. Clearing and overgrazing leave soil bare, so it blows or washes away more easily.
Salinity
salt builds up in the soil and harms plants. Clearing deep-rooted trees or watering crops too much raises groundwater, which brings salt to the surface.
Desertification
dry land loses its plant cover and becomes desert-like. Overgrazing and clearing in dry areas, often along with drought, can cause it.
proposal.remember: Damaged soil grows less food, and the damage often starts with how land is cleared, grazed or watered.
